scientific.integrity: The open-problem statement was inspected in full public text. The closest order-1 radial-center theorem and the cited generalized dual-volume framework were compared at the strongest publicly available statement level. The proof of the new claim is analytic; finite quadrature in the bundled checker is only a regression test.
limitations: The theorem treats Euclidean balls only and does not settle the implication for arbitrary convex bodies.
The one-section equivalence requires ambient dimension at least three.
The radial integral is not affinely invariant, so no ellipsoid extension is inferred.

source_ids: Banach Center Publications 84 (2009), Open Problem Session, Problem 7
title: One-section criterion for Herburt's dual-volume problem on Euclidean balls
